title: Preposizioni Semplici
subtitle: In, a, di, da, su, con, per, tra/fra — Italian's core simple prepositions.
objectives: Use the eight simple prepositions correctly
Distinguish in vs. a for location
Recognize di for possession and origin

content.intro: Prepositions link the pieces of a sentence together — and their use in Italian often doesn't match English word-for-word, so it's worth learning them as fixed patterns rather than translating literally.
content.explanation: The eight simple prepositions are di, a, da, in, con, su, per, tra/fra (tra and fra are interchangeable, chosen just to avoid repeating sounds). In the next lesson you'll see how several of them combine with the definite article (a + il = al) — for now, focus on their use before a noun with no article, and before city names.

rules.heading: a) di — of, from, possession
rules.body:
• Possession: il libro di Marco (Marco's book)
  • Origin: Sono di Torino. (I'm from Turin.)
  • Material: un tavolo di legno (a wooden table)

rules.heading: b) a — to, at, in (with cities)
rules.body:
• Destination/location with cities: Vado a Roma. Abito a Roma.
  • Time of day: a mezzogiorno (at noon)
  • Indirect object: Scrivo a Maria. (I write to Maria.)

rules.heading: c) in — in, to (with countries/regions/enclosed spaces)
rules.body:
• Countries, regions, enclosed spaces: Vivo in Italia. Sono in ufficio.
  • Note the contrast with a: a Roma, but in Italia

rules.heading: d) da, su, con, per, tra/fra
rules.body:
• da — from, since, at someone's place: Vengo da Napoli. Vado da Marco. (I'm going to Marco's place.)
  • su — on: Il libro è su tavolo.
  • con — with: Esco con gli amici.
  • per — for, in order to: Studio per l'esame.
  • tra/fra — between, among, in [time]: tra due ore (in two hours)

examples.it: Sono di Firenze, ma vivo a Milano.
examples.en: I'm from Florence, but I live in Milan.

examples.it: Il gatto dorme su una sedia.
examples.en: The cat sleeps on a chair.
I'm going to Anna's place tonight.
I study Italian with a teacher.

commonMistakes.why: Cities take a for location; in is for countries and regions (Vivo in Italia).
"Going to someone's place" uses da, not a — a is for destinations like cities or specific places, not people.
Di expresses origin ("I'm from..."); a would describe current location, a different meaning.

items.explanation: A for city location, di for origin.

summary: Di = of/from/possession; a = to/at/in with cities; in = with countries, regions, enclosed spaces.
Da = from/since/at someone's place; su = on; con = with; per = for; tra/fra = between/in [time].
The contrast a Roma vs. in Italia is one of the most common early mistakes — learn it as a pair.
